title: Auto-tune signalization for INT8 weight-only profiles and long-run regression suite
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an automated signalization and long-run regression harness for INT8 weight-only quantization profiles (GPTQ/AWQ). The goal is to detect subtle accuracy regressions and stability issues introduced by profile changes, kernel swaps, or hardware differences, and to enable an automated autotune signal that triggers more conservative profiles or falls back to FP16 where necessary. Deliverables: 1) signalization spec and telemetry schema for per-request divergence metrics, latency variance, and kv-cache stability; 2) integration of signals into the calibration pipeline so nightly and canary runs can re-trigger profile sweeps; 3) long-run regression suite that runs simulated production traffic across model variants and hardware types; 4) rollout and rollback playbook with canary thresholds and automatic fallback wiring in the serving runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry events emitted for each inference: token_divergence_score, prefix_stability_ratio, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate
Nightly long-run job executes for at least 12 hours and produces a stability report with pass/fail flags for each profile-model-hardware combination
Canary pipeline ties signal thresholds to automatic profile selection and a documented rollback when divergence_score > 0.02 and p95_latency increase > 25%
Integration tests (synthetic + golden-seed) demonstrate no >1% accuracy delta on a prioritized QA set for the default profile and a documented remediation path when exceeded
Operational runbook created and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML with at least one dry-run canary recorded in PR environment
comments: 2026-02-18 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage — identified need after two post-quant canaries showed intermittent token-level divergence on M4-series hardware. Proposed signalization approach referencing token-level KL and edit-distance proxies. Assigned to Jasper for spike.

2026-02-24 - Jasper Liu: Spike complete. Prototype telemetry events implemented in runtime instrumentation branch (link in attachments). Early results show median token_divergence_score maps to human-evaluated answer deltas. Trade-off: adding per-token divergence increases tracing payloads; plan to sample 1/20 requests in high-volume routes.

2026-03-02 - Riley Chen (Applied ML): Reviewed metric definitions. Suggested replacing raw edit-distance with normalized answer-similarity (BLEU-like) to better capture semantics; noted risk with short responses where BLEU is noisy. Agreed to keep both metrics for 2 weeks, then prune.

2026-03-04 - Jasper Liu: Implemented nightly long-run harness using existing e2e infra. Added synthetic user sessions to reproduce KV-cache ageing. Initial 12h run flagged two model/profile/hw combos with p95 latency spikes; opened ENG-912348 to investigate kernel scheduling under batch fusion.

2026-03-07 - SRE (Carla Gómez): Reviewed canary thresholds. Recommended starting with conservative thresholds (divergence_score 0.03, p95 +40%) for first 3 deploys, then tighten as telemetry confidence grows. Requested logging retention adjustments for 7-day window for root cause investigation.
2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Merged documentation PR and console dashboard mockups. Next steps: wire automatic fallback and create demo runbook for QA to execute in staging next week.
notes: This ticket focuses on end-to-end automation: from telemetry emission to autotune decisioning and regression alerting. It intentionally avoids changing quantization algorithms; instead it stabilizes profile selection and operational detection. The long-run harness should prioritize reproducibility (fixed seeds, controlled session patterns) and surface concise bifurcation points for SRE/ML engineers to act on.
